The core insight is that statue selection in MLB and English soccer is not purely meritocratic but influenced by temporal and affiliative factors. The logistic regression models act as a dual filter: one that evaluates performance and team success (merit), and another that weights loyalty and era (memory). This duality creates a non-linear decision boundary where players with high loyalty and strong historical context are more likely to be honored. The failure mode occurs when either the dataset lacks sufficient representation of certain eras or when loyalty is misinterpreted as a proxy for performance. The mathematical structure of the logistic model allows for probabilistic interpretation of selection outcomes, enabling GSI to compute posterior probabilities of statue depiction given a set of player features. GSE uses this to simulate how changes in era or loyalty might shift the state of statue allocation. The derived kernel is the interplay between historical memory and contemporary performance metrics, which can be encoded as a composite feature vector in both systems.
